context: A uni student interviews a retired diplomat on treaties
purpose: Teach: 安保/締結/国防/是正/阻止/後期/公認/他国

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 今日はお時間ありがとうございます。まず日米安保条約についてお伺いしたいのですが。
lines.en: Thank you for your time today. First, I'd like to ask about the Japan-US Security Treaty.
lines.style: Polite, respectful, slightly nervous opening question from student

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ああ、あの締結の現場には私も若い頃、末席で立ち会ったよ。緊張したものだ。
lines.en: Ah, I was actually present at that signing in my youth, in a junior seat. It was tense.
lines.style: Warm, reflective elder voice with nostalgic gravitas

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 当時、国防の方針を巡って国内で激しい議論があったと聞きました。
lines.en: I've heard there were fierce domestic debates over defense policy at that time.
lines.style: Earnest follow-up showing prior research and curiosity

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: そうだね。条文の不均衡を是正しようと、何度も交渉を重ねたものさ。
lines.en: Indeed. We negotiated repeatedly, trying to correct the imbalances in the clauses.
lines.style: Measured, lecturing tone with hand gestures implied

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 他国の介入を阻止するという目的もあったのでしょうか。
lines.en: Was there also an aim to prevent intervention by other countries?
lines.style: Probing academic question, leaning forward in interest

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: もちろんだ。冷戦後期には、政府公認の極秘協議も水面下で進んでいてね。
lines.en: Of course. In the late Cold War, government-sanctioned secret talks proceeded behind the scenes.
lines.style: Lower voice, conspiratorial but proud, sharing insider history

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: そんな舞台裏のお話、貴重すぎます。論文の核になりそうです。
lines.en: Such behind-the-scenes stories are invaluable. They'll likely become the core of my thesis.
lines.style: Excited, grateful student voice barely containing enthusiasm

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 役に立てば嬉しいよ。歴史は若い君たちが受け継いでこそ、生きるのだから。
lines.en: I'm glad if it helps. History lives only when young people like you carry it forward.
lines.style: Gentle, encouraging closing remark with warm smile
